Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, west Triangle, Quezon City http: //wwvv.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 146 s. 2022 November 15, 2022 Hon. GEMMA G. ADOBO Municipal Mayor Cabucgayan, Biliran Dear Mayor Adobo: This refers to your letter dated 17 August 2022 seeking clarifications on Civil Society Organization Representatives coming from either National Government Agency or BLGU Agency. Per the subject letter, the Municipality of Cabucgayan is in the process of acqrediting the different Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) for membership to the Local Special Bodies. Accordingly, there are various organizations applying and/or reaccreditation in pursuance to DILG Memorandum Circular (MC) No. 2022-083 (Guidelines on the Accreditation of Civil Society Organizations and Selection of Representatives to the Local Special Body). Apparently, during the CSO Assembly held on 5 August 2022, the Resource Person mentioned, citing pertinent provision of the aforesaid MC, that a government employee cannot hold the position of CSO representative in the Local Special Body. Hence, your query—whether or not an employee of the national government agency or a BLGU can sit as CSO representative in local special bodies. In reply thereto, we deem it apt to invite your attention to Article 64 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of the Local Government Code, thus: "Article 64. Procedures and Guidelines for Selection of Representatives of People's Organizations, Nongovernmental Organizations, or the Private Sector in Local Special Bodies- (a) Xxx (b) Xxx (c) Xxx (d) Meeting to choose representatives of people's organizations, NGOs, or the private section- Xxx The selected people's organizations, NGOs or private sector shall then designate their principal and alternate representatives who are residents of the LGU concerned. In no case shall an organization or a "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

representative thereof be a member of more than one local special body within a province, city, or municipality." Now, we go to to Item 4.4.8 of the subject MC in question, thus: "In no case shall the selected representative of an organization be an employee of the provincial, city, or municipal government to avoid conflicts of interest pursuant to Section 1 (1), Rule IX, of the Rules Implementing the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees (Republic Act No. 6713)." The foregoing provisions govern the selection of representatives of CSOs in the LSBs. It is worthy to note that Item 4.4.8 explicitly prohibits any employees of the local governments (whether provincial, city or municipal) from serving as CSO representatives in the LSBs. It is equally important to note that such prohibition was fashioned to prevent potential conflict of interest. It is in this context that this Department opines that employees of the national government agencies may not be allowed to sit as CSO representatives in the LSBs, precisely for the avoidance of conflict of interest. The Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees" (Republic Act No. 6713) defined Conflict of Interest, thus: (i) "Conflict of interest" arises when a public official or employee is a member of a board, an officer, or a substantial stockholder of a private corporation or owner or has a substantial interest in a business, and the interest of such corporation or business, or his rights or duties therein, may be opposed to or affected by the faithful performance of official duty. The Supreme Court has, in several cases it decided, explained the concept of conflict of interest. Accordingly, one of the situations where conflict of interest may arise is when the acceptance of a new relation will invite suspicion of unfaithfulness or double dealing in the performance of one's duty. By analogy, allowing an employee of the national government agency or a BLGU to sit as a CSO representative in LSBs may undermine the operation of LSBs—them being a mere national government employee may unduly influence the decisions of the LSBs, and thus undermine the operation of LSBs. Let it be emphasized that Item 5.8 of the subject MC requires the accredited CSOs to guarantee the autonomy of their organization by not allowing it to be influenced or used for purposes of partisan politics.

This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, By the rity of the Secretary: ATTY. J T R. LLAMAS Und OUS cr tary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs VULLLS-LRALLD/jam Dir. ARNEL M.
